Likely target leakage via near-perfect proxy features

Likely target leakage — the near-perfect R²=1.0 is explained by two features that are essentially transformations of the target: log_target_v2 (Spearman ρ=0.99899) and near_target_proxy (Pearson r=0.99874). These correlations are so extreme that the model is almost certainly reconstructing the target from leaked columns rather than learning a genuine predictive signal.

Model performance for r2=1.0 is leakage-driven. Two features essentially encode the target: log_target_v2 (a log-transformed, versioned copy of the target) has Spearman correlation 0.998993270993271, and near_target_proxy has Pearson correlation 0.998736261844771. All other features have correlations of at most ~0.04 in magnitude, so the perfect R² cannot be attributed to legitimate signal. Although perfect_match_rate is 0.0 (so no row is an exact literal duplicate of the target), the near-perfect correlations indicate the target is recoverable from these derived columns, which explains the suspicious metric.
